title: TAMIU's Ian Rono Earns Second Straight Trip to NCAA Cross Country Nationals
excerpt: TAMIU sophomore Ian Rono earned an individual berth to the NCAA Division II Cross Country National Championships for the second straight year, after finishing 12th at regionals and leading the Dustdevil men to the best regional finish in program history.
content:
Texas A&M International University sophomore Ian Rono is headed back to the NCAA Division II Cross Country National Championships, earning an individual berth for the second consecutive year.

Rono finished 12th out of 169 runners in the men's 10K at the South Central Regional Championships on Saturday, Nov. 21, at the LCU Cross Country Course in Lubbock, posting a time of 30:12.3 and earning All-Region honors for the second straight year, according to TAMIU Athletics.

His run led the Dustdevil men to eighth place out of 24 teams — the highest men's regional finish in program history — with 241 points, ahead of No. 23-ranked Colorado Christian. Freshmen Brian Kipkorir (30th, 31:07.4) and Shamil Kiprono (33rd, 31:17.3) joined Rono among the top 33 finishers.

The team fell one spot short of advancing to nationals as a team — seven South Central programs earned bids — but Rono was one of two individual qualifiers from the region, the NCAA announced Monday, Nov. 23.

As a freshman in 2025, Rono became the first NCAA Division II cross country All-American in TAMIU history, finishing 11th at nationals in 30:02.8.

On the women's side, TAMIU finished 20th out of 24 teams, led by junior Stellah Lagat in 50th with a time of 23:03.6.

The 2026 NCAA Division II Cross Country National Championships are Friday, Dec. 4, at Rim Rock Farm in Lawrence, Kansas. The men's 10K starts at 10 a.m. CST and will stream live on NCAA.com.
